evidence.quote: The language of instruction is half German and half English.
The University of Duisburg-Essen does not charge tuition fees.
Prospective students from non-EU countries submit their application to uni-assist (see application deadline).
Applications for bachelor's programs (including Medicine) are to be submitted through the uni-assist application portal.
Applicants who would like to apply for a Bachelor course as a part of the study program International Studies in Engineering (ISE) must first use the application portal of uni-assist.

note.fr: Vérifiez que votre diplôme de fin d'études secondaires est reconnu comme équivalent au baccalauréat allemand (Abitur) ; sinon un Studienkolleg ou un examen d'aptitutde peut être requis.
note.en: Check that your secondary school certificate is recognised as equivalent to the German Abitur; otherwise a Studienkolleg or a special eligibility examination may be required.

note.fr: Un stage industriel de 12 semaines est obligatoire pendant le Bachelor et doit être prouvé au plus tard lors de l'inscription au mémoire de licence.
note.en: A 12-week industrial internship is compulsory during the Bachelor's programme and must be proven at the latest when registering the Bachelor's thesis.

evidence.quote: During the Bachelor's program, students must complete a 12-week internship.

notes: Application deadlines: the DAAD page gives only 'For the winter semester: 1 May - 15 June' and the UDE pages give general non-EU deadlines ('For courses without admission restrictions: 01 May - 31 July' / 'International: 01.05. - 31.07.'), but these are not explicitly attached to this programme for non-EU applicants in a quotable sentence stating both the period and the applicant group, so no intake was recorded; the programme page indicates unrestricted admission. The semester fee ('about 320,- Euro per semester' / 'about 350 EUR per semester') is an administrative/social contribution, not tuition, and was recorded as tuition 0 EUR. The German B1 and English B1/B2 levels also appear; the DAAD page states German B1 and English B2 for enrolment, while the university pages state B1 in both, with B2 required as a condition of graduation.
